title: Top down shooter basics: aim, bullets and enemies
when: The user wants a top down or twin stick shooter: move with keys or a stick, aim with the mouse or a second stick, and fire at chasing enemies in an arena.
prompt:
Goal: A tight core of move, aim, shoot and dodge with pooled bullets and readable hits.
Steps:
1. Move: normalize the input vector so diagonals are not faster; speed 240 px per second.
2. Aim: angle = Math.atan2(mouseWorldY - player.y, mouseWorldX - player.x), or the right stick when its length passes 0.3.
3. Fire on a cooldown: if (fireHeld && cooldown <= 0) spawn a bullet and set cooldown = 0.12, with a spread of 3 degrees either way.
4. Bullets live in a pool of 256 slots { x, y, vx, vy, life } and are freed on timeout, leaving the arena or hitting.
5. Enemies steer toward the player and add a separation force from neighbors so they do not stack.
6. Hits use circle tests; the enemy flashes white for 60 ms and is knocked back along the bullet direction.
7. After being hit the player blinks with 1 s of invulnerability, plus a 0.1 s slow down.
8. Hide the system cursor over the canvas and draw a crosshair; pointer lock stays optional.
Quality bar:
- Bullets leave from the gun tip, not the player center.
- 300 bullets and 80 enemies run at full frame rate.
Pitfalls:
- A new object per shot, causing garbage collection pauses.
- Aiming with screen coordinates after the camera moved.
- Contact damage on every tick instead of behind a cooldown.
Verify:
- [ ] Diagonal speed equals straight speed.
- [ ] Holding fire gives about 8 shots per second.
- [ ] The bullet pool never exceeds its size.
Output: js/shooter.js (player, bullets, enemies) wired into the loop in js/main.js.

examples.input: jogo de nave visto de cima, mira com o mouse
examples.output: normalized movement, atan2 aim, cooldown fire, 256 bullet pool, separation steering, i frames
